quests.instruction: What gives Earth most of its light and warmth during the day?
quests.hint: Its light is the reason you can see colors outside in the morning.
quests.explanation: The Sun is a star that sends out light and heat. Almost all the energy for life on Earth starts with its light.
quests.funFact: Sunlight takes about eight minutes to travel all the way to Earth.

quests.instruction: Which of these is a living thing?
quests.hint: Look for the one that grows bigger and needs water and light.
quests.explanation: Living things grow, need water, and make more of their own kind. Pebbles and puddles do none of these.
quests.funFact: Some bristlecone pine trees are thousands of years old.

quests.instruction: Drops of water are falling from gray clouds and tapping on the roof. What weather is this?
quests.hint: This is the weather that makes you reach for an umbrella.
quests.explanation: Rain is water that falls from clouds in drops. It fills rivers and soaks into soil where plants can drink it.
quests.funFact: Small raindrops are round, and bigger ones flatten out a bit like tiny buns.

quests.instruction: Look up on a clear night, away from city lights. Which tiny sparkling dots scatter across the dark sky?
quests.hint: Each one is a faraway ball of glowing gas.
quests.explanation: Stars are huge balls of hot gas that make their own light. They look tiny because they are extremely far away.
quests.funFact: On a very dark night you can see a few thousand stars with just your eyes.

quests.instruction: You cannot see it, but you can feel it push your hair and make leaves flutter. What is it?
quests.hint: Kites and sailboats need it to move.
quests.explanation: Wind is air on the move. We cannot see air, but we can see what it moves, such as leaves, flags, and kites.
quests.funFact: Dandelion seeds travel far by floating on the wind.

quests.instruction: Many tall trees grow close together here, and birds and squirrels live among the branches. What is this place?
quests.hint: Walking here feels cool and shady.
quests.explanation: A forest is a large area covered mostly by trees. The leaves and branches give shade, food, and homes to many animals.
quests.funFact: Forests cover about one-third of the land on Earth.

quests.instruction: Which of these holds the most water?
quests.hint: Whales and giant ships need all that room.
quests.explanation: Oceans cover most of Earth's surface and hold most of its water. Ocean water is salty, while ponds and puddles are usually fresh.
quests.funFact: About 7 of every 10 parts of Earth's surface are covered by ocean.

quests.instruction: Which natural material is crumbly and brown, and gives plants a place to hold on with their roots?
quests.hint: Worms wriggle through it, and you get muddy when it gets wet.
quests.explanation: Soil is a mix of tiny bits of rock and rotted plants and animals. It holds water and minerals that plants take in.
quests.funFact: A handful of healthy soil can hold billions of tiny living things.

quests.instruction: Which landform is very tall and steep, with a pointed top called a peak?
quests.hint: The higher you climb it, the colder the air gets.
quests.explanation: Mountains rise far above the land around them. Air gets cooler as you go up, so high peaks can stay snowy.
quests.funFact: Mount Everest, the highest mountain above sea level, is in the Himalayas.

quests.instruction: Which shines in the night sky and looks bigger and brighter than any star?
quests.hint: Its shape seems to change a little each night over a few weeks.
quests.explanation: The Moon looks bright because it reflects sunlight. It does not make light of its own, and it travels around Earth.
quests.funFact: The Moon has no air, so visiting astronauts had to carry their own to breathe.

quests.instruction: Which plant has thin green blades and grows in lawns, parks, and wide meadows?
quests.hint: Cows and sheep love to munch on it.
quests.explanation: Grass grows back quickly after being nibbled or mowed, so grazing animals can eat it again and again.
quests.funFact: Wheat, rice, and corn are all kinds of grass that people grow for food.

quests.instruction: Fresh water that flows along a path from high ground toward the sea is called a...
quests.hint: Follow its current and it leads you downhill.
quests.explanation: A river is moving water that follows the slope of the land. A lake, by contrast, stays in one place.
quests.funFact: Many rivers begin as small streams high up in hills or mountains.

quests.instruction: Sunshine and raindrops together can paint a curved band of colors in the sky. What is it called?
quests.hint: Look for it opposite the Sun, just after a shower.
quests.explanation: Raindrops bend and split sunlight into its colors. You see a rainbow when the Sun is behind you and rain is ahead.
quests.funFact: A rainbow is really a full circle; from the ground we usually see only the top half.

quests.instruction: Tiny grains of broken-down rock and shell cover many beaches. What are they called?
quests.hint: Dry ones trickle through your fingers.
quests.explanation: Waves and wind slowly grind rocks and shells into tiny pieces over a very long time. Those pieces are sand.
quests.funFact: Some beaches have pink or black sand, depending on the rocks and shells nearby.

quests.instruction: Which part of a tree is flat, green, and catches sunlight?
quests.hint: It flutters when the wind blows.
quests.explanation: Leaves catch sunlight, which the plant uses to make its own food. That is why most leaves are broad and thin.
quests.funFact: In autumn, some trees stop making green color, so yellow and red show through.

quests.instruction: Soft white flakes drift down and cover the ground on a very cold day. What is falling?
quests.hint: It turns into water when the weather warms up.
quests.explanation: Snow forms when ice crystals in clouds stick together into flakes and fall through freezing air.
quests.funFact: Every snowflake has six sides or six points.

quests.instruction: After a flash of lightning, you hear a deep rumble in the sky. What is that sound?
quests.hint: When you hear it, it's time to head indoors.
quests.explanation: Lightning heats the air so fast that it bursts outward and makes thunder. Go inside where it is safe during a storm.
quests.funFact: Light travels faster than sound, so you see lightning before you hear the thunder.

quests.instruction: Which of these is a piece of land with water all the way around it?
quests.hint: Boats and planes are the usual ways to reach many of them.
quests.explanation: An island is land surrounded by water. A lake is the opposite: water surrounded by land.
quests.funFact: Hawaii's islands were built by volcanoes that rose up from the sea floor.

quests.instruction: Which animal lives in water, breathes through gills, and steers with fins?
quests.hint: Its body is covered with small shiny scales.
quests.explanation: Fish take oxygen from the water using gills. Rabbits and owls live on land and breathe air with lungs.
quests.funFact: Most fish have no eyelids, so they sleep with their eyes open.

quests.instruction: Bees fly to which part of a plant to find sweet nectar and dusty pollen?
quests.hint: It is often bright or sweet-smelling so that visitors notice it.
quests.explanation: Flowers make nectar, a sweet liquid, and pollen. Bees drink nectar and carry pollen from flower to flower as they go.
quests.funFact: A honeybee can visit hundreds of flowers on a single trip.

quests.instruction: Which landform is a gentle, rounded rise in the land that is lower than a mountain?
quests.hint: You could usually walk up it without climbing gear.
quests.explanation: Hills are rounded and lower than mountains. Rain runs downhill, so streams often begin on hillsides.
quests.funFact: Rain that lands on a hillside can trickle down and start a small stream.

quests.instruction: Which plant has spines and stores water in its thick stem so it can live where rain is rare?
quests.hint: Its prickles keep thirsty animals from nibbling it.
quests.explanation: A cactus soaks up rain quickly and saves it inside its thick stem. Its spines give a little shade and protect it from being eaten.
quests.funFact: Many cacti grow bright flowers, even in hot deserts.

quests.instruction: Inside many fruits are small hard parts that can grow into new plants. What are they?
quests.hint: Plant one in soil, add water, and wait.
quests.explanation: A seed holds a tiny baby plant and a little stored food. With water and warmth it can sprout.
quests.funFact: Orchid seeds are as tiny as specks of dust.

quests.instruction: Which animal has feathers, a beak, and wings?
quests.hint: Many of them build nests to keep their eggs safe.
quests.explanation: Feathers belong only to birds. Butterflies have thin scaly wings, and bats have wings made of stretchy skin.
quests.funFact: A hummingbird can flap its wings dozens of times each second.

quests.instruction: In which season do the leaves of many trees turn yellow, orange, or red and then fall?
quests.hint: The days slowly become shorter and cooler.
quests.explanation: In autumn many trees stop making green color, so the yellows and oranges that were hiding show up. Then they drop their leaves to rest.
quests.funFact: Some trees drop their leaves in the dry season rather than in autumn.

quests.instruction: A large hollow space inside a hillside or under the ground, where bats may rest, is called a...
quests.hint: It's dark inside and the air stays cool.
quests.explanation: Caves form when water or waves slowly wear away rock, or when lava leaves a hollow tunnel behind. Many bats rest in them.
quests.funFact: The temperature deep inside a cave stays about the same all year.

quests.instruction: On a sunny day, a dark shape follows you across the ground. What is it?
quests.hint: It stretches long in early morning and late afternoon.
quests.explanation: A shadow forms when something blocks sunlight. The Sun is low in the morning and evening, so shadows are long then.
quests.funFact: Around midday, when the Sun is highest, your shadow is at its shortest.

quests.instruction: Walking beside a stream, you see many things. Which one was built by people instead of made by nature?
quests.hint: Someone planned it and put it together with tools.
quests.explanation: Rocks, streams, and plants form without help from people. A bridge is built by people to help us cross.
quests.funFact: Animals build too: beavers cut trees to make dams across streams.

quests.instruction: Which place is very dry, gets little rain, and is often covered with sand or rock?
quests.hint: Plants and animals here save every drop of water they can.
quests.explanation: Deserts get very little rain. Plants like cacti and animals like camels have special ways to save water.
quests.funFact: Not every desert is hot: Antarctica is a very cold desert.

quests.instruction: Where a river tumbles over the edge of a high rock, it forms a...
quests.hint: Listen for a roar and look for a cloud of mist.
quests.explanation: Water drops where a river meets a sudden step in the land. Over many years it can wear the rock below into a deep pool.
quests.funFact: Angel Falls in Venezuela is the tallest waterfall in the world.
